historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 8.2% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr 11.0% and EPS 5yr 26.8%. EPS is recovering off a COVID-depressed and pre-restructuring margin base (EBIT margin 9.5% FY2019 -> 23.6% FY2024), so EPS CAGR overstates repeatable growth; equity growth is held down by a rising payout (DPS EUR0.035 -> 0.137). Forward base growth path is set from revenue mechanics (core brands + Versace consolidation), not from either CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF less IFRS-16 lease cash (principal + interest), consistent with lease treatment B; SBC 0 and interest income not deducted (net cash was small vs flows and is gone post-Versace). Owner FCF: FY2021 EUR494m, FY2024 EUR684m -> 3yr CAGR 11.4%. 5yr CAGR not meaningful: FY2019 owner FCF was ~EUR2m (FCF 498.9 less leases 496.5). FY2023 owner FCF was depressed by ~EUR760m capex including flagship real-estate purchases. Reported FCF CAGR is not materially different from owner FCF CAGR (no SBC).

scenario_narratives.base: Miu Miu decelerates from hypergrowth to high single digits while the Prada brand grows low single digits; China stabilises but does not boom. Versace contracts in FY2026 through the creative-director vacuum, dilutes group EBIT margin to ~21%, then is re-launched on Prada's retail and industrial platform and reaches modest profitability by FY2030-31, restoring group reported EBIT to ~23%. Capex stays elevated near EUR550-600m for two years then fades. Group growth fades from 6% to 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Miu Miu keeps compounding as a second scale house (35-40% of retail), the Prada brand returns to mid-single-digit growth as China/APAC recovers, and a new Versace creative director lands well so the brand repeats the Miu Miu playbook (cheaply bought at ~EUR1.25bn vs Capri's $2.15bn). Group EBIT margin moves to ~25% by FY2030 with operating leverage; growth stays above the luxury market for most of the decade. Exit cap 18x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Miu Miu's trend normalises sharply (fashion-cycle risk on a youth-driven brand) while the larger Prada brand stays negative, exposing a one-brand growth story; Chinese luxury demand relapses (APAC ~33% of sales); Versace's turnaround stalls for years and remains loss-making, and group EBIT margin settles ~2-3pp below FY2025. Revenue barely grows in FY2027 after the Versace consolidation step-up. Exit cap 12x for a structurally slower, more cyclical business.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF in EUR at an 8.5% EUR WACC, leases charged as an operating cost, no SBC (cash-settled phantom plans already in EBITDA), Versace priced through the net-debt swing and the FY2026-2030 margin path rather than as a separate asset. Per-share values converted to HKD at EUR/HKD 8.8203 so they are comparable to the HKEX quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Miu Miu growth normalisation -- the single largest swing factor in revenue and margin
Versace turnaround duration: each year of ~-10% Versace EBIT margin costs ~1pp of group margin
Chinese luxury demand (APAC ~33% of retail sales)
EUR/HKD: a 5% EUR move shifts the HKD value 5% one-for-one
FY2025 group cash-flow lines and the June-2026 balance sheet are not on file; net debt is the reported Dec-2025 figure and the gross debt/cash split is estimated
Terminal value cap binds in all scenarios (Gordon at 8.5%/2.5% = ~17x vs 15x cap); the exit multiple is the main terminal judgment

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (1913.HK, HKD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range HK$34.52-52.00. EUR/HKD from Yahoo EURHKD=X; ADR parity via PRDSY.
data_sources.financials: 1913.HK_Metrics.csv FY2018-FY2024 (group annual reports, EUR millions); FY2024 AR cash flow statement for lease principal, lease interest and PP&E D&A; FY2025 separate (parent-only) annual report for Versace financing facilities and outlook (lines 557-570, 1138-1172, 3797-3810).
data_sources.qualitative: 1913.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-17): FY2025 group results (revenue EUR5,718m, adj EBIT 23.2%, net income EUR852m, net financial debt EUR466m), Versace deal terms, FY2026 guidance.

inputs.share_count_basis: 2,558,824,000 ordinary shares, unchanged since the 2011 IPO (FY2024 AR weighted average = basic = diluted). No equity-settled awards (phantom stock plans are cash-settled and already inside personnel cost), no buybacks, no convertibles. Versace was bought for cash/debt, not stock. Held flat.
inputs.sbc_source: No equity-settled SBC: Prada's long-term incentives are cash-settled phantom stock options (FY2024 AR lines 6303, 8477-8493), expensed through personnel cost and therefore already inside EBITDA. SBC-zero market; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fx_note: EUR/HKD 8.8203 (Yahoo EURHKD=X, 2026-10-16T23:14Z). All flows and per-share values computed in EUR and converted at this rate (model -> quote = multiply). Parity check against the OTC ADR PRDSY (1 ADR = 2 ordinary shares): HK$39.22 / (8.8203/1.1244 EURUSD = 7.844 USDHKD) = US$5.00 per share x 2 = US$10.00 vs PRDSY US$10.05 observed (0.5% tie) -- confirms rate, direction and quote basis. Price in EUR terms = EUR 4.45/share; market cap ~EUR 11.4bn.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built: 10y Bund ~2.7% + beta ~1.1 x EUR ERP 5.5% = cost of equity ~8.75%; post-Versace gross debt ~EUR1.8bn at ~3.5% pre-tax (2.5% after 28% tax) against ~EUR11.4bn equity, ~13% debt weight -> WACC ~8.0%; rounded UP to 8.5% for the HKEX-only listing's thin free float (~20%, family holds ~80%). Same 8.5% in all three scenarios: luxury cyclicality, Miu Miu concentration and the Versace turnaround are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. lease_cost_pct_path carries the full IFRS-16 cash lease payment: FY2024 principal EUR438.8m + lease interest EUR69.6m = EUR508.4m = 9.4% of revenue (cash flow statement, FY2024 AR line 5310; lease interest kpi). Lease liabilities (EUR2.38bn at FY2024) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A on PP&E and intangibles only (FY2024 EUR280.5m = 5.2% of revenue, AR line 5276), i.e. ex right-of-use depreciation, so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT. ebitda_margin_path is the post-IFRS-16 EBITDA (FY2024 37.1%).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI immaterial (dividends to non-controlling shareholders EUR0.25m in FY2024); no deduction.
inputs.anchor_vintage_note: FY0 is FY2025 (revenue EUR5,718m incl. ~EUR65m of Versace for December, adj. EBIT 23.2%, net income EUR852m, per the FY2025 results of 5 March 2026 as summarised in the Analysis JSON). The only FY2025 filing on file is the SEPARATE (parent-only) annual report, so FY2025 group cash flow lines are unavailable: last_fcf/reported_fcf are FY2024 group figures (FCF EUR1,192m less lease cash EUR508.4m = owner FCF EUR683.6m, 12.6% of revenue). The component build reproduces ~12% for FY2025, so the anchor is consistent. Net debt EUR466m is the reported FY2025 GROUP net financial debt ex leases (results release). Gross debt/cash split (EUR1,800m / EUR1,334m) is an ESTIMATE: parent third-party borrowings were EUR1,644m at 31-Dec-2025 (separate AR lines 507-517: EUR1,000m 5yr TL + EUR300m bridge + EUR200m 7yr bilateral + legacy) plus ~EUR150m subsidiary debt; cash backed out from the reported net figure. The bridge was refinanced by a EUR300m 10yr USPP in Feb 2026 (neutral to net debt). The 30-Jun-2026 interim balance sheet (post the ~EUR0.42bn May dividend) is not on file; replace at next refresh.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' + adaptations: EUR/HKD dual currency, IFRS-16 lease treatment B, SBC-zero). Prada is a vertically integrated luxury operating company with no bank/REIT/holdco character. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). VERSACE: closed 2-Dec-2025 for ~EUR1.25bn cash, debt-funded; consolidated for one month of FY2025. The acquisition price is therefore already reflected in the EUR466m FY2025 net debt (vs ~EUR607m net cash at FY2024), and Versace's operations enter the flows from FY2026 via the growth path (full-year consolidation of a ~EUR590m revenue brand after a guided contraction from ~EUR684m standalone) and the EBITDA margin path (Versace loss-making, guided dilutive to group EBIT margin in 2026, improvement targeted from 2027). No separate Versace value is added to the bridge -- it would double-count. Buyback cash 0: Prada has never repurchased; the flat count is genuine, not a convention.
inputs.base_revenue_note: PRO FORMA FY2025: reported group revenue EUR5,718m less ~EUR65m Versace December contribution = core EUR5,653m, plus Versace FY2025 standalone ~EUR684m = EUR6,337m. Using the pro-forma base keeps the Versace consolidation step-up out of the growth path, so the working-capital charge (on the CHANGE in revenue) is not levied on acquired revenue whose working capital was bought in the EUR1.25bn price (a first build on the reported base charged ~EUR110m of phantom FY2026 WC build).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +2% on the PRO-FORMA base: core Prada+Miu Miu ~+4% (Miu Miu decelerating from +35%, Prada brand flat, EUR translation headwind) = ~EUR5,880m, plus Versace ~EUR590m after the guided creative-transition contraction from ~EUR684m (-14%) = ~EUR6,470m, i.e. ~+13% on reported FY2025 -- consistent with the mid-teens reported H1 2026 group growth. Then 6% (above-market growth ambition, Versace re-launch) fading to 2.5%.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Post-IFRS-16 EBITDA. FY2024 37.1%, FY2025 ~37% (adj EBIT 23.2%). FY2026 34.8% implies reported-style EBIT ~20.7%: core at ~24% and Versace at roughly -10% (it was loss-making under Capri), matching management's 'dilutive in 2026'. Recovery from 2027 as guided, to 37.4% by FY2031 = reported-style EBIT ~23%, i.e. Versace reaching modest profitability, core flat.
base.capex_rationale: Management's ~EUR500m+/yr strategic investment plan (stores, factories, technology) plus Versace store refurbishment: 9.5% of revenue in FY2026 fading to 7% (FY2024 8.5%; FY2023 16% incl. flagship real estate). Terminal capex 7% vs D&A 6% supports 2.5% growth.
base.wc_rationale: Inventory-heavy vertically integrated retailer: net working capital ~15% of revenue, so growth consumes cash (negative capture).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: group growth now rests on one brand (Miu Miu) whose trend is already decelerating, the Versace turnaround is unproven and started with the creative director leaving within days of closing, and luxury demand is cyclical and China-exposed. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right (Miu Miu durability, Prada-brand recovery, a successful Versace re-launch). Base 50% reflects a balance sheet with no refinancing risk (~0.2x net debt/EBITDA ex leases) and a vertically integrated franchise that has outgrown the sector for four years.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
